overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Council's same-day switch from City Hall to a virtual meeting was adequately advertised through a revised notice with remote access links, the city website, and posted notices at City Hall.

allegations.summary: Council moved its June 22 meeting from City Hall to a virtual Zoom format the same day, with no notice of the change, so members of the public found the building locked.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, on these facts, we find that the Council made reasonable efforts to advertise the change, including by posting a revised notice to the City’s website, which is its official notice posting location, as well as posting notice on all entrances to City Hall where the meeting was originally scheduled to take place.

allegations.summary: Remote access information was not provided to the public when the June 22 meeting became virtual, so the public could not follow it remotely.
allegations.key_passage: The meeting notice included links for a Facebook livestream, a YouTube livestream, and a Zoom meeting, as well as a telephone access number.
